learning_objective: 🎯 Trace the flow of India's rivers! Differentiate between the mighty, snow-fed Himalayan rivers and the older, rain-fed Peninsular rivers.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A 'Catchment area' is where a river collects its water. A 'Drainage Basin' is the entire area drained by a river and its tributaries. A 'Watershed' (or water divide) is the elevated boundary separating one drainage basin from another.

Rivers form geometric patterns based on the land's slope and rock structure. Dendritic looks like tree branches (Ganga). Trellis looks like a rectangular grid. Radial flows outward from a central peak (Amarkantak). Centripetal flows inward to a depression.

Includes the Ganga, Indus, and Brahmaputra. These rivers are 'perennial' (flow all year) because they are fed by both melting snow and monsoon rain. They carve deep V-shaped valleys and form massive deltas at their mouths.

Older than the Himalayan rivers! These include Godavari, Krishna, Cauvery (east-flowing, form deltas) and Narmada, Tapi (west-flowing, form estuaries). They are seasonal (rain-fed) and flow through broad, shallow valleys.

Most peninsular rivers flow East into the Bay of Bengal because the Deccan plateau tilts east. Narmada and Tapi are the exceptions; they flow West into the Arabian Sea through deep rift valleys created by tectonic faults.

fun_activity.title: 🔺 The Delta Builders
fun_activity.instructions: Take a glass of muddy water and pour it slowly onto a flat baking tray slightly tilted into a sink. Notice how the dirt drops out of the water and spreads out in a fan shape right at the edge of the sink? That is exactly how rivers build deltas when they hit the flat ocean!

exam_tips: 📌 A 5-mark question frequently asks you to differentiate between the Himalayan and Peninsular river systems. Use points like origin, nature of flow, type of drainage, and valley shape.
📌 Narmada and Tapi do NOT form deltas; they form estuaries. Be ready to explain this is because they flow through hard rocky rift valleys and don't carry much silt.
📌 The Godavari is the largest Peninsular river system and is often called the 'Dakshin Ganga'.
quick_recap: ⭐ An antecedent river is one that existed before the uplift of the Himalayas and cut deep gorges to maintain its course (like the Indus and Brahmaputra).
⭐ The Brahmaputra is known as the Tsangpo in Tibet, where it carries very little water and silt.
⭐ The entire drainage system of India is roughly divided into the Arabian Sea drainage (23%) and the Bay of Bengal drainage (77%).
